raw_response:
I've been farming these 9 mu for 45 years now. I'm 61, never spent a day in school, but I know this land better than any book. Four of us in the house—me, my wife, my son and his wife—but my son works construction in Handan and only comes back for planting and harvest time. So mostly it's me and the old lady doing the work.

I grow cotton. That's what I've always grown, and that's what I'll grow this year. I don't mess around with new crops. Cotton is money in September and October, as long as the bollworms don't ruin me.

I'll plant around April 20th, when the apricot trees bloom. That's my calendar. I buy improved seed from old Chen's shop in the village—not the fancy hybrid stuff that costs an arm and a leg. About 40 yuan per mu. I plant about 4 to 5 jin per mu by hand.

For fertilizer, I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu before planting—50 jin per mu, the kind with the three numbers on the bag. Costs about 150 yuan. Then when the cotton starts flowering in July, I spread another small bag of urea, about 10 jin per mu. I don't think in kilograms. Old Chen at the shop told me once that it's about 12 kg of nitrogen total per mu, but I just know the plants look greener when I do it this way. I can't afford more than that. Last year fertilizer prices went up, so I cut back a little and the yield was still fine.

Water—I irrigate twice. Once right after planting to get the seeds germinated, and once in late July when the bolls are setting. Pumping from the well costs electricity, and electricity costs money. My neighbor Lao Zhang irrigates three times, but he's got 20 mu and more cash flow. Two times is enough if the summer rain cooperates.

Cotton needs spray, no way around it. I use herbicide once after the cotton comes up, to kill the weeds. Then insecticide three times for the bollworm—early July, mid-July, and early August. The bugs never sleep. I spend about 70 yuan per mu on chemicals.

Tillage? I plow in early spring after the ground thaws, then run the rotary tiller before planting. Same as everyone in the village.

Labor is the hard part. Planting, thinning, fertilizing, spraying—that's all me and my wife. Picking is what kills you. Cotton doesn't ripen all at once. You pick in late September, then again in October, maybe a third time if the weather holds. For 9 mu, that's a lot of bending over. I figure we put in about 20 days per mu of our own work. If we're falling behind during picking season, I hire two women from the east end of the village for a week or so. I pay them 100 yuan per day, plus lunch. That's about 2 hired days per mu over the season.

I expect about 260 kg of lint cotton per mu if the weather is normal. Last year I got about 250 kg/mu. I don't expect miracles. I just want a normal year, enough to cover my costs, pay for my grandson's school supplies, and have a few thousand yuan left for the New Year.

All in all, I'll spend about 4,800 yuan on seeds, fertilizer, chemicals, water, and hired help. That's a big chunk of cash for me. But if I try to save money by skipping fertilizer or spray, I'll lose more in yield than I save. I've learned that the hard way.
